issues.problem: The official Marvel Comics developer API was sunset and is no longer reliably available, so "operational" is incorrect.
issues.suggestion: Set status to "discontinued" and archive or remove the directory entry.

issues.problem: This is the legacy API root of the discontinued service, not a current usable API root.
issues.suggestion: Do not present a current base URL; retain this URL only as historical metadata if discontinued APIs are cataloged.

issues.problem: The free allowance and paid-plan claims are no longer applicable because new access to the API has been discontinued.
issues.suggestion: Set free_tier to false or null and state that the service was discontinued.

issues.problem: The 3,000-calls-per-day limit describes the former service and is no longer a current usable quota.
issues.suggestion: Set to null or "not applicable; service discontinued."

issues.problem: The request is no longer usable against a dependable official service, and the response snippet is also missing the final closing brace for the top-level JSON object.
issues.suggestion: Remove the live example or label it historical; if retained, append the missing closing brace.

issues.problem: The Stocks Basic free plan provides end-of-day data, not 15-minute-delayed stock data. Delayed data is associated with a paid Stocks Starter plan.
issues.suggestion: Use "5 API calls/minute; end-of-day US stocks; 2 years of historical data" and separately describe the other asset-class free plans.

issues.problem: The stated paid-plan limits of 100, 500, and 1,000 calls per minute are outdated. Current individual Stocks Starter, Developer, and Advanced plans advertise unlimited API calls, while Basic remains 5 calls/minute.
issues.suggestion: Use "Stocks Basic: 5 API calls/minute; paid individual Stocks plans: unlimited API calls, subject to plan terms and fair-use controls." Verify other asset classes separately.

issues.problem: The Bearer value is labeled YOUR_API_KEY even though Mastodon authenticates API calls with an OAuth access token, not an API key.
issues.suggestion: Change the header to "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN".

issues.problem: Matrix has no universal matrix.org API root, and matrix.org currently advertises https://matrix-client.matrix.org as its client API base through .well-known discovery.
issues.suggestion: Use "https://{discovered-homeserver-base}/_matrix/client/v3" generically, or "https://matrix-client.matrix.org/_matrix/client/v3" specifically for matrix.org.

issues.problem: The example bypasses Matrix homeserver discovery and uses the outdated matrix.org host. It also labels the Bearer credential as an API key rather than an access token.
issues.suggestion: Use "curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN\" \"https://matrix-client.matrix.org/_matrix/client/v3/account/whoami\"" for matrix.org, or substitute the discovered homeserver base.

issues.problem: The entry conflates paid GeoIP web services at geoip.maxmind.com with the separate free GeoLite web service at geolite.info. GeoIP is pay-per-query apart from a limited trial; GeoLite provides 1,000 free queries/day.
issues.suggestion: For this GeoIP2 base URL, set free_tier to false and list current per-query prices: Country $0.0001, City Plus $0.0003, and Insights $0.002. Mention the $5 trial separately. If an ongoing free tier is desired, create a GeoLite entry using https://geolite.info/geoip/v2.1.

issues.problem: The placeholder "..." supplies no valid limit and obscures the distinction between products. Paid GeoIP web services do not advertise a routine query quota, although MaxMind may temporarily rate-limit excessive erroneous requests; GeoLite is limited to 1,000 queries/day.
issues.suggestion: Use "GeoIP: no published routine query-rate quota; excessive error traffic may be rate-limited. GeoLite: 1,000 queries/day."

issues.problem: curl interprets the unescaped square brackets in filter[stop] and page[limit] as URL-globbing syntax and exits with a bad-range error.
issues.suggestion: Percent-encode the brackets as filter%5Bstop%5D and page%5Blimit%5D, or add curl's --globoff option.

issues.problem: The claim that the free tier is HTTP-only is outdated. The current Free plan includes HTTPS encryption.
issues.suggestion: Use "100 requests/month; delayed news data; HTTPS included; no historical data or commercial use."

issues.problem: The Wikimedia-specific statement is outdated: Wikimedia introduced published request limits in 2026. Current limits include 10 requests/minute for unidentified clients, 200/minute for identified unauthenticated clients and many authenticated users, and 2,000/minute for established authenticated editors, with specified exemptions.
issues.suggestion: State the current Wikimedia limits while retaining that independently hosted MediaWiki installations can configure different limits.

issues.problem: Current Wikimedia API policy requires an identifying User-Agent with contact information; the example relies on curl's generic default User-Agent and may be throttled or blocked.
issues.suggestion: Add a header such as "-H \"User-Agent: ExampleApp/1.0 (contact@example.com)\"".
